title: Register Avatar Accessory
content: #### Register an avatar accessory file or convert a pattern into an accessory. ![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44760225403161) [Watch Video](https://youtu.be/TApSQk7tXUY?si=MWBU0VR5tacpweKs) 1. Open the avatar file to register an accessory. 2. Click Main Menu » Avatar » **Register Accessory**. 3. After setting the options below, click the Save button. **Menu** | **Description** ---|--- **Basic** | **Accessory Type** | Select the type of the accessory.(Hair, Shoes, Earring, Glasses) **Object** | Select the type of the object (file and pattern) to register. You can load and select objects in the 3D window and adjust their positions directly. **File** | Select the path to the hair and shoe files to register. **Scale/ Axis Conversion** | Change the size and axis of the loaded file and check it simulatenously. **Pattern** | Select the pattern you want to convert to the accessory. However, the pattern to be converted must be created in advance before the accessory registration is proceeded. **📝****Note:** After selecting the pattern to be converted to an accessory, you can also right-click the 3D pattern ▶ Convert ▶ to Avatar Accessory menu. **Option** | **Mirror Creation** | If you register shoes and earrings, it automatically creates the opposite object. Inverted relative to the central axis of the avatar. **Thumbnail** | **Auto** | Apply the thumbnail image automatically. **Custom** | Apply the desired image as the thumbnail. 4. Click**Save** button to save as the Avatar Accessory file. #### **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44760225407513)** Easily register shoes without limitations like left/right distinction or heel assignment. 1. Set Accessory Type to **Shoes** **» Heels** in Register Accessory window. 2. When opening a shoe file, CLO will automatically differentiate between the left and right shoes. 3. For heels, follow these steps to ensure a proper fit: 3-1. In the 3D window, click on the heel meshes of the shoe. If the heel has multiple meshes, select them all at once by clicking and dragging to define the area. 3-2. Right-click and click **Set as Heels**. If incorrectly set, right-click and click **Unset Heel.** **![Shoes.gif](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44762280722841)** 4. Click**Save** button to save as the Avatar Accessory file.
content_description: Easily register and convert accessory files for avatars, including shoes and patterns, with step-by-step instructions and video support.

title: Graphic Properties
content: **List of Contents** **Set Properties** **Set Options** **** Set the graphic properties. #### **Set Properties** ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/51790077104665) **By Graphic Style;**_Applies changes to all graphics that use the same style._ 1. Click the Graphic Style in the Graphic tab in the Object Browser. 2. Set properties in the Property Editor. **Properties** | **Description** ---|--- **Information** | **Name/Item No.** | Enter a name or an item number of the graphic. **Classification** | Assign the graphic type among Embroidery, Logo, Print, Wash (Jeanologia). **Teckpack** **(CLO-SET)** | Check whether to include the graphic in the tech pack. Assign the classification of the graphic as per its purpose. **Material** | **Print Type** | Set the print type of the graphic (Crack, Vintage Distress, Golden Foil). When you select the Blend with Base Fabric type, all PBR maps (Normal, Displacement, Opacity, Roughness, Metalness maps) of the fabric applied to the pattern are automatically applied and blended with the fabric. Otherwise, you can selectively apply only specific maps by checking the 'Use the same map as the fabric' option for each map. Set the graphic's [material](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115015998728-%EC%9E%AC%EC%A7%88-%EC%9C%A0%ED%98%95), [texture](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000471388-%EC%9B%90%EB%8B%A8-%ED%85%8D%EC%8A%A4%EC%B2%98-%EB%84%A3%EA%B8%B0), [color](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/sections/115000716427-%EC%9B%90%EB%8B%A8-%EC%83%89%EC%83%81), and [transparency](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000512488-%ED%88%AC%EB%AA%85%EB%8F%84-%EC%84%A4%EC%A0%95). **Graphic Transformation** | Adjust the width and height of the graphic to transform its size. ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/51790077104665) **By Each Graphic;**_Applies changes only to each selected graphic, even if they share the same style._ __ 1\. Click the Graphic using ![Transform Graphic.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53267500551833) **Transform Graphic** tool in the 2D toolbar. **Properties** | **Description** ---|--- **Graphic Configuration** | **Face** | Place the graphic on the front, back, or both sides. **Tile** | Repeat the graphic in its original size along the X-axis, Y-axis, or across the entire pattern. **Over Seamline** | Place the graphic on the seam of patterns. \- Graphic does not appear when the difference of the seam is over the allowable extent. \- Graphic may not be matching when it is placed over the curves. It this case, deactivate this option and adjust the graphic manually. \- Graphics are also created for patterns sewn in two layers, such as pockets.[![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/26258156519577) Watch Video](https://youtu.be/bV6e36l_95A?si=AWD9r_QdGkHTvdJB&t=4271) **Graphic Transformation** | Adjust the rotation angle and Z-offset of graphic. **2D Measurements** | Click the desired measurement option to check the position within the 2D pattern in dimensions. **Transform Graphic** | ![20252.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/51790282286105) Precisely place graphics by entering exact position values. #### **Set Options** 1. Right-click on the Graphic using ![Transform Graphic.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53267500551833) **Transform Graphic** tool in the 2D toolbar. 2. Select the option as needed. **Options** | **Descriptions** ---|--- **Delete** | Delete the selected graphic. **Copy/ Paste** | Copy, Paste, and Mirror Paste the selected graphic. **Order (2D)** | Set the placement order of the graphic. **Rotate** | Set the rotation angle of the graphic. **Tile** | Repeat the graphic in its original size along the X-axis, Y-axis, or across the entire pattern. **Revert to Original Size** | Restore the transformed graphic to its original size. **Flip** | Flip the graphic horizontally or vertically. **Trace as Internal Shape** [![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/26258156519577) Watch Video](https://youtu.be/3FTUcfpFrWI?si=j50eaGqv_JOeGc_Y) | Trace the graphic as an internal shape according to its outline. **📝Note:** The clearer the image, the more accurately it is recognized. For complex and colored images, tracing is based on the outermost outline. **Custom Measurements** [**![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/26258156519577)**Watch Video](https://youtu.be/u3AWgMtT_9U?si=mkdbFzGglJTUaSY9&t=199) | Measure the distance from a specific point of the graphic to its outline and create a measurement. The created measurement is displayed in the Property Editor, and you can rename or delete it as needed.
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide for setting and customizing graphic properties and options within your design software, enabling users to efficiently manage and transform their graphics.

title: Rotate Dart
content: Move a dart to a new location or divide it by rotating it. **Please note that this option only appears if both sides of the dart are the exact same length.** **Rotate to a New Location** 1. Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit**▶ Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar **▶![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/36791106874009) Edit Pattern** 2. Right-click after selecting both segments of a dart. → A right-click pop-up menu appears. 3. Select **Rotate Dart** and click on the pattern outline to draw a new dart location. → The centerline of the original dart appears as a guideline. 4. Click on the guideline to set a pivot point. → The pattern is divided into two parts. 5. Click and move the mouse towards the direction where the selected part should rotate. → The dart is rotated to the selected location. 6. Move the mouse cursor along the new dart's centerline to set its length. → The dart is completely rotated with the new length. **Rotate into Another Dart** 1. Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit**▶ Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar **▶![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/36791106874009) Edit Pattern** 2. Right-click after selecting both segments of a dart. → A right-click pop-up menu appears. 3. Select **Rotate Dart** and click another dart's intersection. → Both segments of the dart are automatically selected. → The pattern is divided into two at the intersection of two darts' centerlines. 4. Click and move the mouse towards the direction where the selected pattern should rotate. → The dart is rotated to the selected location. 5. Move the mouse cursor along the new dart's centerline to set its length. → The dart is completely rotated with the new length. **📝****Note:** * Right-click while rotating or setting the length to input specific values. * When rotating darts, a baseline is automatically generated on the rotated dart.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for rotating and repositioning darts in a 2D pattern, ensuring precise adjustments while maintaining symmetrical lengths.

title: How can I change or reset my password on CLO Web and the Software?
content: **Question** How can I change or reset my password on CLO Web and the Software? **Answer** To change or reset your password, go to the Account page on CLO website. How to reset your password varies depending on the version of your software. Please select your option below: * CLO version 2024.0 and above: Change CLO-SET password * CLO version below 2024.0: Reset Software password * Reset website password: Forgot my password ![account-EN.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/34001101960473) #### #### **CLO version 2024.0 and above** Please click on the 'Change Password from CLO-SET' button on the Account page, and you will be redirected to the 'My Page' section of CLO-SET, where you can change your password. #### **CLO version below 2024.0** Please click on the 'Reset password' button in the CLO License Password box on the Account page. * If you have CLO-SET account and are using a version of the software below 2024.0, your license password will not be synchronized with the password of your CLO-SET account. #### **Forgot my password** If you are already a member of CLO-SET, please follow the indicated guideline below: 1. Please sign in with CLO-SET option. 2. Then, click on the '[Forgot your password?](https://style.clo-set.com/en/account/password/find?returnUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fclo3d.com%2Fauth%2Fsignin%3FredirectTo%3D%2F&uaa=1)' button. 3. Enter an email address to receive a link to reset your password. 4. Check your email and follow the directions indicated in the email. If you haven't integrated your account with CLO-SET yet, please follow the indicated guideline below: 1. Navigate to the [sign-in page](https://www.clo3d.com/signin) on CLO website. 2. Click on the "[Forgot your password?](https://www.clo3d.com/en/signin/cant-signin)" button. 3. Enter an email address to receive a link to reset your password. 4. Check your email and follow the directions indicated in the email. *If the account is locked after entering the wrong password five times, please use the “Find Password” and “Reset Password” options to regain access. *If you are unable to access your email to reset your password, please reach out to CLO via [Contact Us](https://www.clo3d.com/support/contactus) page.
content_description: This page provides step-by-step instructions for changing or resetting your password on CLO Web and the software, tailored to different versions and scenarios.

title: My order seems wrong. Whom should I contact?
content: **Question** My order seems wrong or unintended. Whom should I contact? Where can I check my inquiry status? **Answer** 1. CLO provides an auto-renewal system for Individual plans and notifies individual users of it on the checkout page before a subscription. 2. CLO sends an email about the renewal notification 5 days before auto-renewal. *If you don't want to renew your subscription, you can cancel your subscription on your order page of CLO web. 3. If your subscription is renewed successfully but cannot access CLO, your invoice might be processing, causing the access issue. In this case, please wait a bit and check your renewal invoice is issued through your email box. Then, you can access CLO software. 4. After sending your inquiry, you can check the inquiry status in the **Request History Button![Request History button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53137207475609) **of your account page. 1. If you see that your inquiry status is SOLVED, this means internal agents have replied to your question. However, if you cannot get a response from us, please try to resend your inquiry. However, when you experience any unintended payment, please [contact us](http://clo3d.com/contact) with your payment information.
content_description: This web page provides guidance for users experiencing issues with their orders, including how to contact support and check the status of inquiries related to subscription renewals and payments.

title: How do I download the installer?
content: **Question** How do I download the installer? Where can I download the installer by versions? **Answer** #### **Before You Begin** *Before downloading, you must purchase a license or try a free trial. Otherwise, even if you have the software, you may not be able to access it or see a deactivated button on the download page. *Users who created a CLO account as of March 19th, 2024 can only download version 2024.0.1 or higher installers. #### **CLO for Individuals** To download an installer by version: 1. Sign in and navigate to the [Download Page](https://www.clo3d.com/en/clo/download) on the footer. * You must use 'Sign in with CLO-SET' for the 2024.0.1 installer or above. 2. You can find the download buttons for PC or MAC (the latest version) if you have an active subscription. 3. You can also click '[CLO Installer](https://clo3d.com/en/clo/download/installer)' for the old version. * Select the Standalone Onlineauth tab for Individual licenses. #### **CLO for Enterprise and CLO for Academic Institution** To download the installer: 1. If you want to get the installer download link for Enterprise/Academic Institutions, please [contact us.](https://www.clo3d.com/support/contactus) Our business development team will provide you with more information. #### ****Recommended Default Installation Paths** **Windows:** Installing under C:\Program Files is the standard practice. **macOS:** The typical installation path is /Applications. Using the default installation path ensures that the operating system properly recognizes the program and maintains compatibility with built-in features and components.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for downloading the CLO software installer by version, along with essential pre-download requirements and recommended installation paths.

title: I cannot log in. What should I do?
content: **Question** I cannot log in. What should I do? I cannot sign in on the CLO web or CLO software, even if I enter a valid ID and Password. I was charged for my subscription, but it says I don't have a license **Answer** Please follow the instructions below based on your subscription plan and software authentication for Business Plan Clients to solve the login issue. **CLO for Individuals** 1. Please use the Chrome browser over other browsers and remove the old cookies. 2. Check your user ID and Password (User ID and PW you set up when signing up clo3d website.) -For signing in to CLO software, the user ID is your email address above CLO 2024 version, or the name on your account page or receipt below 2024 version. -If you receive the user ID as your email address, please install CLO software with 2024 version via the [download page](https://clo3d.com/en/clo/download) and access CLO software through 'sign-in with CLO-SET'. -Please check your user ID from your subscription invoice as some users are confused with other CLO accounts. 3. Please check if you access the CLO software for an Individual license (Standalone Onlineauth). 1. If the CLO software is not Standalone Onlineauth, please go to the download page after signing in and install the right version. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/52747524784537) 4. If the PC's 443 port firewall is blocked, unblock and try logging in again. 5. Deactivate the antivirus program on the PC and try logging in again. 6. If the above steps do not solve your problem, please reach out via [Contact Us](http://clo3d.com/contact). **CLO for Business Users** **Standalone** 1. Check the dongle key is connected to the PC, and try logging in again. 2. Check the [HASP Driver](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000615488#Click3) is properly installed, and try logging in again. 3. Confirm internet connection. 4. Confirm ID and Password. 5. If the PC's 443 port firewall is blocked, unblock and try logging in again. 6. Deactivate the antivirus program on the PC and try logging in again. 7. If the above steps do not solve your problem, please reach out via [Contact Us](http://clo3d.com/contact). **Network** 1. Check the dongle key is connected to a PC in the same network service, and try logging in again. 2. Check the [HASP Driver](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000615488#Click3) is properly installed on the PC, and try logging in again. 3. Check your computer is in the same network service as the PC with the dongle key. 4. If your computer is not in the same network service, select port forwarding and try logging in again. **OnlineAuth** 1. Confirm ID and Password. 2. If the PC's 443 port firewall is blocked, unblock and try logging in again. 3. Deactivate the antivirus program on the PC and try logging in again. 4. If the above steps do not solve your problem, please reach out via [Contact Us](http://clo3d.com/contact).
content_description: This webpage provides troubleshooting steps for users experiencing login issues with CLO software, including guidance for both individual and business subscription plans.

title: Edit 3D Garment
content: **List of Contents** Edit Style Line Scale/ Move Style Line Draw Style Line **Objective** Edit 3D garment easily by moving point and line by keeping its shape. **** **Location** 3D Toolbar **▶![Scale StyleLine.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53431208484249) Edit StyleLine **Tool 3D Toolbar **▶![Scale StyleLine.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53431208484249) Scale StyleLine **Tool 3D Toolbar **▶![Add StyleLine.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53431224771481) Add StyleLine **Tool ## **Operation** **Edit Style Line** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated. 2. Click on the 3D garment to be edited. → Pattern outline and point appear with a black outline. 3. Click on the point ▶ drag and move. → The line and the point sewn are moved together. 4. Or click on the segment ▶ drag it. → The curvature of the line is now adjustable. **Scale/ Move Style Line** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated. 2. Click on the 3D garment to be edited. → Pattern outline and point appear translucent. 3. Click on the segment ▶ drag it. → The garment is scaled or moved with the sewn lines in the drag direction. **Draw Style Line** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated. 2. Click on the 3D garment to be edited. → Pattern outline and point appear translucent. 3. Hover on a Segment, a blue point will appear, click to start the new Style Line. → A point is added to the selected point. 4. Draw a curved line by clicking within the pattern piece, then double click on the segment where you want the new Style Line to end, or draw a straight line by double-clicking the endpoint. → The pattern piece cut along the style line added. **※ Note:** \- The function that allows you to scale or move one side of the sewn lines is excluded in the 6.2 version. The new feature with the improvement of usability will be provided. \- While Editing/Scaling/Moving Style Line, right click to enter the desired dimension. (ver 7.1)
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for efficiently editing, scaling, and drawing style lines on 3D garments using the 3D Toolbar.

title: Smooth Curve
content: Round the corner of Patterns and Internal Shapes. 1. Click ![Smooth Curve.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53430948374809) **Smooth Curve** in the 2D toolbar. 2. Click and drag a corner or a curved segment to be rounded. 3. Right-click while dragging the point or the curved segment to enter the desired line length and curvature. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44891633367833)** ## ![Update.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44891633371801) Curvature of a specific line can be precisely adjusted without affecting other lines. 1. Click a start point and endpoint on the segment or point to set the editing range. 2. Select which side to be edited. 3. Click and drag a segment or point to adjust curvature within the set range. **Edit** • By default, nearby points adjust proportionally when moving. You can move only the selected point by holding the Ctrl key while dragging. • Right-click while dragging the segment or point to enter a specific moving distance. **Add** • Click a segment whild holding the Ctrl key to add a curve point. _*Adding to a Bezier curve points convert it to free curve points, which may adjust the curvature._ **** **Delete** • Right-click a point and click the Delete menu to delete selected points. 4. Or click and drag a reference line to replace it with a new curve. 5. Press Enter to complete. → When selecting a pattern outline or internal line, update based on the edited pattern outline or internal line. → When selecting a reference line, update based on the edited reference line. Segment points will be added at the start and end.
content_description: Learn how to expertly round corners and adjust the curvature of lines in your designs using the Smooth Curve tool in Clo3D.

title: [2D Tool] Segment Sewing
content: ### **Objective** Establish Sewing Lines on segments of Patterns or Internal Shapes/Lines. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D ▶ Sewing ▶ **Segment Sewing** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001250948/_______.png) **Segment Sewing** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D ▶ Sewing ▶ **Segment Sewing** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001250948/_______.png) **Segment Sewing** 2. Click once on the Pattern segment to establish the first half of the seam. 3. With the mouse cursor, hover over the segment to be sewn to the first half of the seam. Drag the mouse to make the Directional Notches parallel to each other. Then, click to establish the second half of the seam. **※ Note** * When Directional Notches are crossed, the Sewing Lines in the 3D window are crossed as well. When Patterns are simulated at this state, either one of the Patterns is reversed and then sewn to the other Pattern. * Use the shortcut to establish M:N Sewing Lines. For more details, please reference [M:N Segment Sewing](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000497727).

title: CLO to MetaHuman: USD Garment Integration Workflow
content:
This guide outlines the entire workflow for exporting garments from Marvelous Designer as USD and integrating them with Unreal Engine **MetaHuman**. * * * ### **⭐1. Project Initialization and Plugin Setup** #### **1-1: Installing Core Data** Ensure you have **Unreal Engine 5.6** or later installed before proceeding. 1. Open the **Epic Games Launcher** and navigate to the **Library** tab. 2. Locate your Unreal Engine installation card. 3. Click the **down arrow** next to the **Launch** button and select **Options**. 4. In the installation options window, check the box next to **MetaHuman Creator Core Data**. 5. Click **Apply** to download and install the required data. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53323164145945) #### **1-2: Project Configuration** 1. Create or open your Unreal Engine project. 2. Navigate to **Edit > Project Settings** in the main menu. 3. In the left sidebar, scroll down to the **Plugins** section and select **MetaHuman SDK**. 4. Locate the setting labeled **MetaHuman Packaging Paths**. > **⚠️ Warning:** **Do not change the name of this folder path.** Due to a known issue, the workaround currently in place relies on this folder retaining its default name. Modifying it will break the packaging process. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53323158561817) #### **1-3: Outfits Directory Setup** By default, the location for Outfits is `/Game/Outfits`. In your **Content Browser** , this path appears as **All > Content > Outfits**. You should create and edit all your Outfit Assets within this directory. **Important for FAB Uploads:** If you plan to use the **MetaHuman Manager** to verify and package your asset for FAB, you must adhere to a strict folder structure: * Your Outfit Asset and **all of its dependencies** must reside in a single subfolder within the `/Game/Outfits` directory. * If assets are scattered outside this specific subfolder, the MetaHuman Manager will fail the verification process, and packaging will be impossible. #### **1-4: Plugin Setup** Make sure to enable **Chaos Cloth Plugins** and **MetaHuman Creator Plugin** , and restart your Unreal Engine project. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53323164146329) ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53323164146585) * * * ### **⭐2: Preparing MetaHumans for Export (UE 5.6 and later)** #### **2-1: Create and Customize the MetaHuman** 1. In the **Content Browser** , right-click and navigate to **MetaHuman > MetaHuman Character**. 2. Open the newly created MetaHuman asset to enter the editor. 3. Customize the character’s attributes (Face and Body Measurements) as needed. #### **2-2: Configure Assembly Settings** Once customization is complete, prepare the asset for export: 1. Navigate to the **Assembly** tab. 2. Select **Download Textures**. 3. Check the box for **Create Full Rig**. 4. Change the Assembly Target from **UE Cine (Complete)** to **(DCC Export)**. 5. Select your desired **Output Folder**. 6. Click the **Assembly** button to generate the files. > **ℹ️ Integration Note:** Successfully completing this step saves the specific Body and Head files required for **DNA Import in CLO**. You will need this DNA file in the next section to accurately fit garments to your MetaHuman body. * * * ### ⭐**3: Import MetaHuman DNA into CLO (CLO 2025.2 or later)** 1. Launch **CLO**. 2. Navigate to **File > Import > DNA** in the main menu. 3. Browse to the output folder you defined in the previous section. 4. Select the exported **Body** and **Head** files. 5. Click **OK** to complete the import. For more details, please refer to the following CLO manual for more details: [**MetaHuman DNA Importer**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/51821648831257-MetaHuman-DNA-Importer) * * * ### **⭐4: Prepare Garment in CLO and Bake UV Maps** #### **4-1: Garment Simulation** 1. Create a new garment or apply existing garments. 2. Run the Simulation to drape and fit the garments onto the imported MetaHuman body. #### **4-2: UV Preparation** Before exporting, ensure the UV maps are correctly packed to prevent texture issues. 1. Switch the view to the **UV Editor**. 2. Select the **whole garment** (all patterns). 3. Run **UV Packing** to organize the UV islands efficiently. #### **4-3: Exporting to USD files** 1. Navigate to **File > Export > USD**. 2. In the export dialog window, configure the settings exactly as follows: **Setting Category** | **Configuration** ---|--- **Object** | Select **Include Garment** **Patterns** | Choose **Select All Patterns** **Geometry** | Set to **Single Object** **Thickness** | Select **Thick** **Textures** | Check**Unified UV Coordinates** and **Select All Maps** **Simulation** | Check **Include Garment Simulation Data** * * * ### **⭐5: Convert Style into a Resizable MetaHuman Wardrobe Asset** #### **5-1: Prepare Project and Import USD Outfit** **Step 1: Open Your Project** Launch Unreal Engine 5.6 (or later) and open your target project. **Step 2: Establish Directory Structure** You must establish a precise folder hierarchy in the **Content Browser**. This structure is critical for asset validation. 1. Navigate to `/Game/Outfits/`. 2. Create a folder named after your asset (e.g., `Style01`). 3. **Crucial Step:** Inside that folder, create a **subfolder with the exact same name** (`Style01`). Your hierarchy should look like this:
```
Content
└── Outfits ├── Meshes <-- Store MetaHuman (MH) skeletal files here └── Style01 <-- Main Asset Folder └── Style01 <-- Working Folder (Import USDs here)
``` **Folder Purpose Definitions:** * **Meshes:** Dedicated storage for MetaHuman skeletal and mesh files. * **Main Folder (e.g., Style01):** This parent folder will eventually contain _only_ the finalized wardrobe asset. * **Working Folder (e.g., Style01/Style01):** This is your workspace. All development, importing, and editing must take place here. You may organize subfolders inside this directory as needed. **Step 3: Export the MetaHuman Reference Mesh** You need the skeletal mesh from your MetaHuman to serve as a reference. 1. Navigate to your MetaHuman asset location. 2. Locate the **Skeletal Mesh** for the body (not the Blueprint). 3. Right-click the asset and select **Asset Actions > Export**. 4. Save this file to the `Outfits/Meshes` folder you created in Step 2. **Step 4: Import the USD Outfit** 1. Navigate to your working folder: `Outfits > Style01 > Style01`. 2. Import your USD outfit file into this folder. 3. In the **USD Import Options** dialog, leave all settings at their **Default** values and click **Import**. Unreal Engine will automatically generate subfolders for _Textures_ , _Materials_ , and _Static Meshes_. Locate and double-click the **Static Mesh** of the outfit to open it. **🔧 Troubleshooting: Transparency Issues** If your garment appears transparent or ghostly in the viewport, follow these steps to fix the material blend mode: 1. In the details panel or content browser, find the material applied to the mesh. 2. Right-click the material instance and select **Find Parent**. 3. Open the Parent Material. 4. Scroll down to the **Material Property Overrides** section. 5. Locate **Blend Mode**. 6. Change the dropdown from **Translucent** to **Opaque**. 7. **Save** and **Apply** the material. #### **5-2: Create and Configure Cloth Asset** **Step 1: Create the Cloth Asset** First, you need to generate the base asset files in your project directory. 1. Navigate to your **Working folder**. 2. **Right-click** > **Physics** > **Cloth Asset**. 3. Name the asset clearly (e.g., `CA_Style01`). > **Note:** This automatically creates a **DataFlow node** with a "DF" prefix. This node is required for the asset to function—do not delete or modify it. **Step 2: Open and Clean the Dataflow Graph** Set up the workspace by removing unnecessary simulation nodes. 1. **Right-click** on your new CA Node (`CA_Style01`). 2. Select **Open in Dataflow Editor (Experimental)**. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53335888520729) 3. **Clean up the graph:** Since you are not running a simulation, delete all nodes **EXCEPT** the following: * `Transfer Skin Weights` * `Remesh` * `ClothAssetTerminal` * _(Optional)_ You may also delete the purple and brown explanatory notes. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53335876830233) **Step 3: Import and Connect Static Mesh** Now, import your specific outfit geometry and establish the node connections. 1. **Add Import Node:** Right-click in the graph, type **StaticMeshImport** , and select it. 2. **Configure Node Details** (Bottom-right panel): * **Uncheck:** `Import Sim Mesh` (as you do not have one). * **Static Mesh:** Drag in or select your outfit mesh (e.g., `style01`). 3. **Connect the Nodes:** * Drag from `StaticMeshImport` (**Collection**) → `TransferSkinWeights` (**Collection**). * Drag from `TransferSkinWeights` (**Collection**) → `Remesh` (**Collection**). * Drag from `TransferSkinWeights` (**Collection**) → `ClothAssetTerminal`. * Drag from `Remesh` (**Collection**) → `Collection Lods 1` (on the Terminal node). **Step 4: Configure Skin Weights** Adjust the `TransferSkinWeights` node to map the outfit to the character body correctly. 1. Click on the **TransferSkinWeights** node. 2. Update the **Node Details** panel with the following settings: * **Target Mesh(es):** Change to `Render Mesh`. * **Render Mesh Transfer Source:** Change to `Skeletal Mesh`. * **Transfer Method:** Change to `Closest Point on Surface`. * **Source Asset:** Drag in or select the combined body mesh paired with the garment (e.g., `Character01_CombinedSkelMesh`). **Step 5: Visualize the Asset** Verify your work in the Construction Viewport. 1. Click on the **Remesh** node in the graph. 2. Locate the **Construction Viewport** (the window to the _left_ of the Simulation Viewport). 3. If the viewport is empty: * Click the **View Mode Dropdown** (Top right of the viewport, icon looks like a cube). * Select **Render**. 4. Save Project. #### **5-3: Create and Configure Wardrobe Asset for MetaHuman Creator** **📂Step 1: Organize Folders** Before starting, ensure your file structure is clean to avoid referencing errors. 1. Navigate to your main folder → **Style01**. 2. Ensure this folder contains **only** your **Working folder** (which should be named identically to your intended outfit asset or use the `OA_` prefix). 3. Remove any other loose assets or extraneous folders. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53335845173657) **👕Step 2: Create the Outfit Asset** Generate the core asset file using the physics menu. 1. **Right-click** in the folder → **Physics** → **Outfit Asset**. 2. **Name the Asset:** * Must match your folder name exactly. * _Recommended Format:_ `OA_Style01`. 3. **Select Template:** * Choose **Resizable Outfit** when prompted. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53335817349529) **📦Step 3: Manage the Dataflow (DF) Node** A dependency node is automatically created and must be stored correctly. 1. Locate the new node prefixed with `DF_`. 2. Drag it into your **Working folder**. 3. Select **Move Here**. > **Note:** This step is required for packaging in Fab and ensuring compatibility with the MetaHuman Manager. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53335849553433) **⚙️Step 4: Configure the Dataflow Editor** Open the editor and optimize performance settings before adding heavy assets. 1. **Double-click** your new Outfit Asset (`OA_Style01`) to open the Dataflow Editor. 2. Locate the **Evaluate Dataflow Graph** button in the top toolbar. 3. Click the **three dots** next to it. 4. Select **Manual Graph Evaluation**. * _Why?_ This prevents the engine from trying to process changes after every single click, avoiding long wait times during setup. **🧵Step 5: Add Cloth Assets** Link your Cloth Assets (CA) and Skeletal Meshes to the Outfit Asset. 1. **Dataflow Members Panel** (Bottom Left): * Check the box for **Sized Outfit Source**. * Click the **Plus (+)** sign for each cloth asset you need to add. 2. **Configure Each Entry:** * **Source Asset:** Select your cloth asset (e.g., `CA_Style01`). * **Size Name:** Enter a descriptive name. * **SourceBodyParts:** Add your combined skeletal mesh (e.g., `Character01_combinedSkelMesh`). * **Num Resizing Interpolation Points:** * _Default:_ 1500 * _Recommended Range:_ 1000–2500 * _Tip:_ Higher numbers are more accurate but process slower. 3. **Variable Overrides:** * Switch to the **Dataflow Tab** (Bottom Left). * Find **Variable Overrides** and check the box for **SIZE OUTFIT SOURCE**. * Verify that both the `CA_` asset and the `CombinedSkelMesh` are successfully linked. **⏳Step 6: Evaluate the Graph** Process the data to generate the outfit sizes. 1. Click **Evaluate Dataflow Graph** in the top toolbar. 2. **Wait:** Watch the progress bar as it processes each size. This may take several minutes. 3. **Reset:** Once complete, click the three-dot menu again and turn **Automatic Evaluation** back on. **🔄Step 7: Re-Evaluation (Troubleshooting)** If you modify any input assets later (cloth, static mesh, etc.), you must force a re-evaluation. 1. Click **Evaluate Dataflow Graph**. 2. **If no progress bar appears:** * Right-click the **Sized Outfit Source** node → **Evaluate**. * _OR_ Right-click the **OutfitAssetTerminal** node → **Evaluate**. **💾Step 8: Save** * **Save your Outfit Asset** to preserve all configurations. **👤Step 9: Test in MetaHuman Creator (MHC)** Verify the outfit works on a character and resizes correctly. 1. **Create Test Character:** * Content Browser → Right-click → **MetaHuman** → **MetaHuman Character**. * Name the character. 2. **Open in MHC:** * Open the character and navigate to the **Hair & Clothing** tab. * Scroll to **Outfit Clothing**. 3. **Apply Outfit:** * Remove the current **Wardrobe Asset**. * Drag your **Outfit Asset** (`OA_Style01`) into this slot. * Double-click to apply. 4. **Test Resizing:** * Use body sliders or apply different presets to ensure the clothing adapts to the body shape. **🧥Step 10: Verify Wardrobe Item** * After applying the outfit, check your Content Browser. * A new asset should appear: `WI_Style01` (Wardrobe Item). * * * ### **⭐6. MetaHuman Outfit Testing Checklist** The following checklist provides quality assurance for the MetaHuman testing phase. Use this to systematically verify that your `OA_` asset resizes correctly without breaking. **1\. Preparation** * [ ] **Clean State:** Ensure the character has no other clothing layers underneath that might cause false clipping positives. * [ ] **Asset Applied:** Verify `OA_Style01` is successfully slotted in the **Outfit Clothing** section. * [ ] **Visibility:** Zoom in close to the garment boundaries (necklines, cuffs, waistbands). **2\. The "Extremes" (Stress Testing)** _This is where most resizing errors occur. If it works here, it usually works everywhere._ * [ ] **Maximum Bulk:** Set sliders/preset to **Tall + Heavy/Overweight**. * _Check for:_ Skin poking through the cloth (clipping) at the stomach, shoulders, and thighs. * [ ] **Minimum Frame:** Set sliders/preset to **Short + Thin/Underweight**. * _Check for:_ "Floating" geometry where the cloth is too far from the skin, or collapsing geometry where the mesh overlaps itself. **3\. Specific Body Regions** _Adjust individual sliders if your interface allows, or select specific presets._ * [ ] **Chest/Bust:** Maximize and minimize. Check for texture stretching or distortion on logos/patterns. * [ ] **Shoulders:** Widen and narrow. Check if straps (if applicable) stay aligned or slide off. * [ ] **Waist/Hips:** Check the transition area. If this is a shirt, ensure it doesn't clip into the pants line (or vice versa). **4\. Visual Inspection Criteria** * [ ] **Clipping:** No skin showing through the fabric. * [ ] **Distortion:** No extreme stretching of the UVs/texture (e.g., plaid patterns looking like spaghetti). * [ ] **Seams:** Ensure the vertices at the seams are not splitting apart during resizing. * [ ] **Neckline:** Ensure the collar doesn't eat into the neck on "Heavy" settings. **5\. Final Verification** * [ ] **Reset to Neutral:** Return to **Average Height + Average Weight**. Does the mesh snap back perfectly? * [ ] **Asset Generation:** Confirm that the `WI_Style01` (Wardrobe Item) exists in the content browser after your tests.

title: Modes

title: Why do I have to pay tax?
content: **Question** I am VAT registered. Why do I have to pay tax? **Answer** Please note that if you have a correct registered VAT ID, you can add VAT ID on Billing Address and your tax will be waived. Since January 2019, CLO Virtual Fashion LLC (CLO US office) has officially been registering VAT MOSS (Sales Tax) in Ireland (Europe). Since our online license sales are handled by our US office, all of our Individual license pricing will be in effect according to the regulation below. From January 2015, new legislation came into force that affects the sale of digital services to customers in other EU countries. Digital services include broadcasting, telecommunications, and electronic services (which includes software products). The VAT rate that is calculated for this type of transaction is based on the place supplying the service. The legislation that is regulating MOSS rules is: * [Council Directive (EU) 2017/2455](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:32017L2455&from=EN) \- Supplies of services and distance sales of goods (VAT e-commerce package). * [Council Directive 2008/8/EC](http://eur-lex.europa.eu/LexUriServ/LexUriServ.do?uri=OJ:L:2008:044:0011:0022:EN:PDF) \- Place of supply of services. * [Council Implementing Regulation (EU) No 1042/2013](http://eur-lex.europa.eu/LexUriServ/LexUriServ.do?uri=OJ:L:2013:284:0001:0009:EN:PDF) \- Place of supply of services. This means if your billing address is in the European region, VAT rates for each country will be added to your purchase. Austria | 20% ---|--- Belgium | 21% Bulgaria | 20% Croatia | 25% Cyprus | 19% Czech Republic | 21% Denmark | 25% Estonia | 20% Finland | 24% France | 20% Germany | 19% Greece | 24% Hungary | 27% Ireland | 23% Italy | 22% Latvia | 21% Lithuania | 21% Luxembourg | 17% Malta | 18% Netherlands | 21% Poland | 23% Portugal | 23% Romania | 19% Slovakia | 20% Slovenia | 22% Spain | 21% Sweden | 25% United Kingdom | 20% If you would like to discover more regarding VAT MOSS, please review the file attached.

title: Sew Blocks
content: **List of Contents** Sew Patterns and Block Boxes Show Modular Sewing / Show Pattern Sewing ### **Objective** Set seamlines between Patterns and Block Boxes. **Location** Modular Mode ▶ **Block Editor** **Operation** **Sew Patterns and Block Boxes** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ **Block Editor** 2. Click on******![Segment Sewing.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53165021281305)****Segment sewing** tool or ![Free Sewing.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53165036872089) **Free sewing** tool. 3. Set seamlines for Pattern and its relative Block Boxes (Step 2 and 3 do not necessarily need to be in order). 4. Set Pattern outlines (Patterns must be sewn one another i.e. shoulder seams, armholes, side seams) and seamlines between Block Boxes. 5. Repeat the steps above for the remains. **※ Note:** * Block Boxes can only be sewn with **Segment Sewing**. In other words, sewing multiple Block Box segments at once by using **M:N Free Sewing** is not allowed. Therefore if the number of Block Box segments is higher than the number of segments need to be sewn, add segments on the patterns to make the number equal, then sew them 1:1. ex) In case of a basic t-shirt block, there is a point added on the neck segment. Therefore add a point on its pattern, then sew the segments 1:1. * Patterns that are sewn alone (i.e. hems, sleeves or armholes of a sleeveless style) do not need to be sewn to Block Boxes. * Difference in length between the actual Pattern and the Block Boxes has no effect on the simulation. * Rest of the principle is the same as the Simulation Mode. **Show Modular Sewing / Show Pattern Sewing** 1.
